Need the patient's fluorescein angiography and OCT angiography reports to definitively confirm retinal vein occlusion versus neovascular age-related macular degeneration, as these are the core missing examinations for verifying the leading hypothesis of cystoid macular edema secondary to retinal vein occlusion.

Need the fluorescein angiography and OCT angiography findings from the available evidence texts to confirm retinal vein occlusion as the cause of cystoid macular edema and exclude neovascular age-related macular degeneration, as these are the decisive missing examinations.

bindings.label: Persistent vision loss in the right eye for 1.5 years
63-year-old male with medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and multiple strokes
Visual acuity in the affected eye ranged between 20/100 and 20/200
Ophthalmoscopic examination revealed severe macular changes with associated edema
OCT shows persistent cystoid macular edema with central thickness 669.8 μm over 12 visits
Cystoid macular edema was documented to reverse after stopping niacin
Fluorescein angiography and OCT angiography were not performed
No clinical or laboratory evidence of intraocular inflammation was found
Right eye cystoid macular edema secondary to retinal vein occlusion
Right eye neovascular age-related macular degeneration
Patient had been taking niacin before discontinuation
Right eye niacin-induced cystoid macular edema
